errors.text: The hypothesis changes the material from a lamellar FCC/B2 Al0.7CoCrFeNi eutectic high-entropy alloy to an unspecified refractory BCC/B2 high-entropy alloy.
It proposes generic inverted-microstructure engineering rather than the required HPHT treatment at 6 GPa and 1473 K for 2 hours.
The predicted improvement concerns compressive ductility, whereas the question requires room-temperature tensile ductility and strength.
It does not address dislocation pile-ups, boundary stress concentrations, dislocation transfer, interfacial microcracking, or catastrophic tensile fracture.
The cited evidence supports inverted BCC/B2 refractory alloys but provides no evidence that this intervention applies to the specified FCC/B2 eutectic alloy.
